senses.definition: (archaic) A supercilious or haughty attitude; arrogance.

quotes.text: They being newcomers, free from the western morgue so soon caught by Oriental Europeans, were particularly civil to me, even wishing to mix me a strong draught; but I was not so fortunate with all on board.
quotes.reference: 1855, Sir Richard Burton, Personal Narrative of a Pilgrimage to Al-Madinah and Meccah, Dover, published 1964, page 34:

senses.definition: A building or room where dead bodies are kept before their proper burial or cremation, (now) particularly in legal and law enforcement contexts.
(archaic) The archive and background information division of a newspaper.

quotes.reference: 1921 July 2, Joseph F. Kwapil, Fourth Estate, page 5:

quotes.text: Shand: get down to the Record and the Trib. See what they've got on Elliot in their morgues.
